title: Tool session sentinels and idempotent replay protocol for multi-tool chains
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Users can create orchestrations that call multiple tools in sequence while streaming partial outputs back to clients. Current executor prototypes handle chaining and naive result injection but are brittle under replays, partial failures, and duplicated tool invocations. This ticket implements a compact session sentinel and idempotent replay protocol so the executor can: 1) identify a logical tool session across retries and resumptions, 2) attach deterministic idempotency keys to injected results, and 3) stream stable, ordered events to callers even when underlying tool runs are retried or reordered.
acceptance_criteria: Executor attaches a stable session-sentinel header (session_id + version) to every tool invocation and persisted replay record.
Tool results include an idempotency_key derived from (session_id, tool_index, invocation_hash) and are deduplicated by the executor before injection.
Streaming API maintains monotonic event sequence numbers per session; clients can resume from last-seen sequence number and receive no duplicated injected results.
Latency and tail-percentile regressions are within 5% of current baseline for common chat+tool workloads (100k message sample), validated in canary.
Automated chaos tests (network partitions, duplicate events, tool-side retries) pass in CI with zero data corruption and clear observability traces.
Design doc and security assessment completed and linked; implementation passes code review and unit/integration tests.
design_notes: Session sentinel: 128-bit stable session_id (uuidv7 recommended) + 8-bit protocol version. Sent as executor header X-Redwood-Tool-Session: <session_id>:<ver>.
Idempotency key derivation: HMAC-SHA256(secret_key, concat(session_id, tool_name, tool_index, canonicalized_input)) then base64url-truncate(18) to keep key compact for logs and storage.

Replay log: append-only event stream per session in local durable store (RocksDB) keyed by session_id; each event has seq_no (u64), idempotency_key, event_type (invocation|partial_output|final_output|error), tool_metadata, and a small provenance blob (tool_runtime, start_ts, end_ts).
Deduplication window: executor keeps a 24-hour TTL index of seen idempotency_keys per session; memory-bounded LRU + periodic compaction for long-running sessions.

Streaming contract: server-sent events (SSE)/gRPC stream messages include seq_no, event_kind, idempotency_key (optional for partial_output), and payload. Clients resume by providing last_seq_no and session_id; executor replays missing seq_no events from replay log.

Fallback behavior: if a tool fails with non-retriable error, executor emits a terminal error event with code and suggestions; if retriable, uses exponential backoff with jitter and preserves original idempotency_key so retries dedupe at injection point.

Compatibility layer: add shim to accept legacy requests without session header; shim will allocate ephemeral session_id and mark session_version=0. This preserves backward compatibility with older SDKs.
Security: idempotency HMAC uses per-cluster secret rotated via KMS; logs redact canonicalized_input for PII-sensitive tools. Security review required for cross-tenant leak risk in shared caches.
tradeoffs: Write-ahead replay log simplifies resumability but increases disk I/O; mitigated by batching writes and compacting events after final_output acknowledged.
Long TTL for dedupe improves safety for slow tools but increases storage; chosen 24h as pragmatic middle ground based on observed retry windows.
Using HMAC-based idempotency avoids requiring tool-side cooperation but introduces KMS rotation complexity and per-cluster secret management.

Generating session IDs at executor edge for legacy clients ensures compatibility but prevents client-side deterministic resumption across different executor instances unless caller migrates to SDK supporting explicit session header.
rollout_plan: Feature branch -> unit tests -> integration tests against local executor harness.
Canary deploy to runtime-1.20-canary region with 5% traffic for 48 hours; monitor seq_no gaps, duplicate-injection rate, and streaming latency.
If canary is green, progressive rollout 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 1 week with health checks and automated rollback on error budget breach.
Expose opt-in SDK flag (enable_session_sentinels) and default to false for two cycles; flip default after two successful releases to avoid unexpected behavior for existing customers.
Post-rollout: run migration script to compact replay logs older than 7 days and publish runbook for on-call when session-level stalls occur.
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency_key derivation and canonicalization of tool inputs (edge cases: unicode, whitespace, nested JSON ordering).
Integration tests: end-to-end chat + two-tool chain with intermittent tool failures; assert no duplicate injections and correct ordering.
Chaos tests: simulate duplicate tool callbacks, network partition between executor and replay store, and ensure stream resumption works from last_seq_no.
Performance tests: compare p50/p95 token latency on representative workload (chat with small tools) against baseline; goal <5% regression.
Security tests: ensure canonicalized_input redaction for flagged tools, KMS rotation exercises do not invalidate existing idempotency_keys incorrectly.
review_comments: 2026-03-05 - PM review (Liam O'Connor): 'Love the session sentinel approach. Please add an explicit metric for duplicate-injection-rate and a dashboard query example.'
2026-03-08 - Design review (Priya Menon): 'Consider making seq_no monotonic per executor shard as well as per session to ease debugging; avoid relying solely on session-local counters.'
2026-03-10 - Security (Darren Wu): 'HMAC key handling looks good; require token-scoped KMS keys for enterprise tenants to prevent cross-tenant replay risk.'
2026-03-12 - Engineering (Miguel Torres): 'Implemented draft in branch feat/session-sentinels. Initial integration tests pass; need to tune RocksDB write batching and add compaction job.'
